# external.ipdsc__v1

## Purpose
**IPDSC = "IP → Data Source Category":** the resolved, materialized map of which category ids each IP
belongs to, per data source, per day. It is the join surface the **MNTN Match (MM) batch
prospecting-scoring** pipeline reads to score households/IPs, and the surface that audience-segment
eligibility and impression enrichment match against (impression ⋈ targeted segment ⋈ IPDSC). Reach for
it to answer "was this IP a member of category C under data source N on day D?" — the addressable
universe behind a prospecting audience expression. CRM (DS4) membership that never lands in the segment
snapshots (`raw.tmul_daily` carries only DS2/DS3) is resolved through the identity graph into IPDSC.

GCS backing: `gs://mntn-data-archive-prod/ipdsc/*` (Parquet), hive-partitioned `dt=<date>/data_source_id=<n>/`.
Registered as an EXTERNAL table in `dw-main-bronze.external` (job location `us-central1`).

## Grain & keys
- **Grain:** one row per (`ip` × `data_source_id`) within a daily `dt` partition. The row's
  `data_source_category_ids` is the **array of every category id that IP maps to** under that source that
  day (one row already carries all of an IP's categories for that source — categories are the array, not
  separate rows).
- **Natural key:** (`ip`, `data_source_id`, `dt`).
- **Join columns:** `ip` (→ impression/bid IP), `data_source_id` (→ `integrationprod.audience_data_sources`),
  `data_source_category_ids.list[].element` (→ per-source category catalog: `fpa.categories`,
  `bronze.tpa.categories`, `external.tpa__sharethis_categories__v1`, `external.tpa__dstillery_categories__v1`).

## Column meanings (only the non-obvious ones)
- `ip` — the IP address (STRING, dotted IPv4 e.g. `1.112.130.245`). This is the identity grain — IPDSC is
  keyed on IP, not on any advertiser/campaign/household id. Match to impression/bid IP for enrichment.
- `data_source_category_ids` — Parquet list-of-struct: `STRUCT<list ARRAY<STRUCT<element INT64>>>`. The
  category ids this IP belongs to under `data_source_id`. Unnest as
  `UNNEST(data_source_category_ids.list) AS c → c.element`. The ids are the **per-source
  `data_source_category_id`** and are hierarchical — a leaf co-occurs with its parent (e.g. `101` +
  `101001`, `104` + `104014`). Decode against the source-specific catalog, NOT a single global taxonomy.
- `dt` — partition column, **STRING date `YYYY-MM-DD`** (a hive-partition value, not a TIMESTAMP/epoch).
  Daily snapshot. Always filter it.
- `data_source_id` — partition column, INT. The originating data source (DS). Decode via the authoritative
  registry `dw-main-bronze.integrationprod.audience_data_sources` (`data_source_id → name/display_name`).
  Well-established members seen here: **4=CRM**, **13=MNTN Vertical Categorization** (aka "Peak
  Performance"/Jaguar intent), **14=freshness / recently-seen-IP gate** (~149M IPs/day, ~8-day serving TTL;
  materialized here since AUDI-369), **16=advertiser's own funnel/delivery tags** (Impressions/Wins/per-
  CampaignGroup — not a buyer audience), **17=ShareThis 3P interest**, **18=Dstillery 3P interest**,
  **19=MNTN Matched keyword/product categorization** (RTC/MM), **35=LiveRamp IP (3P)**, **46=Fangorn
  vertical-anchor**, **47=CRM-upload exclusion lists**, **51=Bombora B2B intent** (began delivering IPDSC
  volume ~2026-07-06). Others present (2, 8, 9, 42, 43, 49, 63) decode via the registry. **Oracle (DS1) is
  NOT in IPDSC** — legacy/deprecated, still selectable in the buyer UI (dead-weight clauses).

## Joins & relationships
- **Impression / bid fact → IPDSC** on `ip` (+ `data_source_id`, + a `dt` lookback window). This is the
  eligibility/enrichment join. **Fan-out warning:** the fact side is the many side; one IP appears in
  IPDSC once per (data_source_id, dt), so joining across multiple `dt` days or multiple data sources
  multiplies rows — constrain `dt` to the intended lookback and filter `data_source_id` first.
- **Category decode** — explode `data_source_category_ids.list`, then join `element` →
  the per-source catalog keyed on `data_source_category_id` within that `data_source_id`
  (DS13/14/16/21 → `fpa.categories`; DS17 → `tpa__sharethis_categories__v1`; DS18 →
  `tpa__dstillery_categories__v1`; DS35 → `bronze.tpa.categories`).
- **`integrationprod.audience_data_sources`** — 1:1 decode of `data_source_id` → source name.
- **Sibling `external.ipdsc_geo__v1`** — the geo-partitioned companion under the same
  `gs://mntn-data-archive-prod/` archive (separate table, not documented here).
- **Consumers:** MM batch scoring (produces household_score); impression enrichment
  (`impression_enrichment` config `ipdsc_lookback=35` → 35-day window); audience segment eligibility
  (impression ⋈ `summarydata.v_campaign_group_segment_history` ⋈ IPDSC, ~30-day lookback).

## Gotchas
- **Rolling archive, not a full history.** GCS retains ~90 daily partitions
  (`dt=2026-04-29 … 2026-07-28` as of 2026-07-29 = 91 days). Old `dt` partitions age out; do not assume
  arbitrary historical dates exist. Confirm the date exists before querying.
- **The data-source SET grows over `dt`.** Earliest partition had 15 sources; latest had 18 — new DS feeds
  (e.g. DS51 Bombora ~2026-07-06, DS9/63) appear only from their onboarding date forward. A missing
  `data_source_id=N` partition for a `dt` means "no delivery that day" (Bombora drops ~every other day →
  0 DS51 that dt; self-heals next delivery), not zero members — **absence ≠ empty**.
- **`data_source_category_ids` is REQUIRED (mode NO)** but its inner `list` array can be present-yet-short;
  always unnest via `.list` — a bare reference returns the struct, not the ids.
- **Categories are already aggregated per IP.** One row = all of an IP's categories for that source that
  day. Do NOT expect one row per category; a `GROUP BY ip` is unnecessary within a single (dt, DS).
- **`ip` is the only identity.** No advertiser_id / campaign_id / household_id here — segment/advertiser
  scoping happens downstream in the audience-expression + scoring layer, not in IPDSC.
- **No CDC hygiene columns** (`deleted`/`is_test`) — external GCS Parquet; none apply.
- **`dt` is a STRING** — compare as `dt = '2026-07-28'` / `dt BETWEEN '…' AND '…'`, never as a DATE/epoch.

## Cost & partitioning notes
- **Hive-partitioned on `dt` AND `data_source_id`** — filtering BOTH prunes GCS objects and is the primary
  cost lever. `require_partition_filter` is not enforced on an external table, but a scan without a `dt`
  (and ideally `data_source_id`) filter reads the entire `gs://mntn-data-archive-prod/ipdsc/` tree — very
  expensive. **Always filter `dt`; filter `data_source_id` whenever you know the source.**
- **BQ cannot pre-estimate federated bytes:** `bq show` reports `numRows=0`/`numBytes=0` and a `--dry_run`
  reports a 0-byte lower bound (verified) — these are external-table artifacts, not empty data. Judge cost
  by partition scope (days × sources), not the dry-run estimate.
- **Volume is large per day.** DS14 alone is ~149M IPs/day; a single full `dt` across all sources is
  hundreds of millions of rows. Prefer one `dt` + one `data_source_id` + a `LIMIT`/aggregate; never scan
  the whole archive to learn a column.
- Narrow table (4 columns); `SELECT` only what you need and unnest categories lazily.

## Example queries
```sql
-- Categories for one source on one day (partition-pruned), exploded
SELECT ip, c.element AS data_source_category_id
FROM `dw-main-bronze.external.ipdsc__v1`,
     UNNEST(data_source_category_ids.list) AS c
WHERE dt = '2026-07-28'
  AND data_source_id = 13
LIMIT 100;

-- Is a given IP in any DS35 (LiveRamp) category over a 3-day window?
SELECT dt, ip, ARRAY_LENGTH(data_source_category_ids.list) AS n_categories
FROM `dw-main-bronze.external.ipdsc__v1`
WHERE dt BETWEEN '2026-07-26' AND '2026-07-28'
  AND data_source_id = 35
  AND ip = '1.112.130.245';
```
